edits.paragraph_text: Objective. To quantify spatial population structure, gene flow and candidate signatures of local selection in Plasmodium falciparum across Ghana's agro-ecological zones using the MalariaGEN Pf8 release; to measure the zone-level frequencies of the canonical antimalarial resistance codons, and the haplotypes they form within isolates; and to establish whether zone-level differentiation is detectable at all before any locus-specific signal is interpreted.
edits.context_before: Abstract
edits.context_after: Design limits, stated first. Zone is not an isolable variable in this dataset. Three of the four represented zones are each filled by exactly one administrative region (Guinea savanna / Upper East, coastal savanna / Greater Accra, transitional zone / Brong Ahafo); collection year differs systematically between zones; and four of the six zone pairs share no Pf8 sequencing study at all, including coastal savanna versus Guinea savanna, the pair that carries every headline number. Ecology, administrative region, collection period and sequencing batch are collinear by construction. Every zone-level result below is a statement about that compound variable. It is arranged broadly from south to north, but not monotonically: the transitional zone is the second-most-northern of the four and is represented by only 25 analysed isolates, and it breaks the south-to-north ordering in all but one of the variables examined here - the single exception is pfaat1 S258L, which declines monotonically from coastal savanna through deciduous forest and the transitional zone to Guinea savanna - so no claim of a latitudinal cline is made from the four zone means alone. No adjustment within these data can decompose the compound variable.

edits.context_before: [Interpreted] Conclusion. At the resolution these data permit, Ghanaian P. falciparum shows very low but statistically detectable differentiation at the retained common variants. Five of the six pairwise estimates have 95% confidence intervals excluding zero; only Guinea savanna against the transitional zone, where n = 25, spans it. Very low is not the same as undetectable, and neither is a demonstration of random mating, for which these data contain no direct evidence. What the sensitivity analysis adds is stability of the magnitude rather than absence of the effect: the maximum pairwise FST stays within 0.00204-0.00255 across all six threshold scenarios, over 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs, so the headline result is insensitive to both of the cuts that define the dataset. The companion claim does not survive the same treatment. The region-level isolation-by-distance result is significant at the published thresholds and at MAF >= 0.02, but in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, and this report therefore no longer asserts a distance effect, weak or otherwise. What remains of the spatial signal is a single south-to-north contrast, visible in the FST ranking and in the K = 2 minor component, with no robust evidence that genetic distance scales with geographic distance. That very low differentiation is a statement about neutral common-variant structure only: neutral common-variant differentiation between zones is negligible, so a spatially sparse design is adequate for characterising neutral structure, but marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and the resistance panel in this analysis shows significant between-zone variation at p < 0.001 at pfdhfr, pfdhps and pfaat1. That threshold is stated because it is a selection: on the four-zone chi-square as reported, several further loci are nominally significant at p < 0.05, among them pfcrt I356T (p = 1.6 x 10 to the -3), pfmdr2 I492V (p = 0.020) and pfmdr1 N86Y (p = 0.029). Low neutral FST therefore does not license an assumption that marker frequencies are spatially representative. The pfk13 result is a genuine tested negative - no screened resistance allele occurs at any of the 23 codons, which cover the complete WHO-validated set of 14 and all 6 candidates: twenty-two are fixed at the reference residue and codon 458 is at 0.9995 on a single Asn458Asp call, which is not the validated N458Y, on 1,845 to 1,876 isolates called per codon - rather than an untested absence; it is also a statement about 2009-2021 and not about current parasite populations. The XtX set remains a ranked candidate list, of which 13 SNPs survive FDR 10% and two adjacent chromosome-11 sites - one of them the fifth-ranked SNP overall - are flagged lower confidence on ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff grounds. All zone-level results describe a compound variable in which ecology, administrative region, collection period and sequencing study cannot be separated; that is a property of the Pf8 metadata, not of the analysis.

edits.paragraph_text: Malaria transmission in Ghana is spatially heterogeneous, and the heterogeneity tracks ecology. The country spans a south-to-north gradient of agro-ecological zones that differ in rainfall, vector species composition, seasonality and consequently in entomological inoculation rate. If parasite populations in these zones are demographically separate to any meaningful degree, then drug-resistance alleles, antigenic variants and locally adaptive alleles can differ in frequency between them. If instead the zones exchange parasites freely, an allele arising anywhere will spread everywhere, and the surveillance question becomes one of timing rather than of geography.

edits.paragraph_text: [Interpreted] A refinement of the framing. An earlier version of this report ran the argument directly from the amount of neutral structure to a conclusion about surveillance design - that if the parasites form one population, spatially sparse sentinel sampling is representative. That step does not hold, and the project's own literature review argues against it: selection builds connectivity and locus-specific allele trajectories that neutral demography does not predict, so a resistance allele can have a site-specific frequency even under neutral panmixia. Neutral differentiation and marker-frequency representativeness are two distinct quantities and have to be measured separately. This analysis therefore does both - genome-wide differentiation at common variants, and direct resistance-marker frequencies by zone - and reports them as two findings rather than deriving the second from the first.

edits.context_after: Scope. The thesis proposal and literature review (supplied separately as "genomic analysis of Consistent signatures of selection.docx", 145 paragraphs, approximately 11,400 words) set out the biological rationale, the resistance-marker panel and the published context. This report does not restate that material. It documents what was computed, on what data, with which decisions, and what the output actually shows, following a full re-run of stages 4-9 in which seven defects were fixed: six identified by adversarial audit, and a seventh found by the re-run itself. The seventh is the more instructive one and is claimed here rather than buried. The "skip if output exists" guards in step05b, step07b and step08b did not check whether their inputs had changed, so when the SNP set went from 3,359 to 3,916 both ADMIXTURE and TreeMix silently re-reported the previous day's results as "stage finished". Only step08c caught it, because it asserts that its position table and the BayPass output have matching row counts and so failed loudly with the right diagnosis; ADMIXTURE and TreeMix have no such assertion. The guards now require each output to be newer than its input. The audit did not raise this defect.

edits.paragraph_text: [Interpreted] A fifth round, and the loss of a result. Four outstanding robustness checks were run at final revision, and they are the reason this version grades one finding lower than the last. Three of the four left the conclusions standing or strengthened them: the maximum pairwise FST varies only between 0.00204 and 0.00255 across six threshold scenarios spanning 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs, so near-panmixia does not depend on the Fws or MAF cuts; the 19 XtX outliers are better-supported calls than the rest of the scanned panel rather than artefacts, although two adjacent chromosome-11 sites are downgraded within that set; and re-running the ordinations on the 1,900-isolate analysis set, so that they describe the same isolates as everything else, changes nothing material. The fourth check overturned a conclusion. The region-level isolation-by-distance result - the only positive spatial finding in this report - is significant in 2 of those 6 threshold scenarios and in 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, collapsing when Upper East is dropped, and is therefore graded not robust wherever it appears below. It is not deleted: it holds at the published thresholds, and it is reported together with the scenarios in which it fails. But it can no longer be described as supported, moderately supported, or a weak but real distance effect, and the preceding version's listing of it among the strengthened results is withdrawn. The remaining check, the provenance of the agro-ecological zone layer, cannot be closed analytically at all and stays open.
edits.context_before: [Interpreted] A later round, and a fourth consecutive correction containing its own defect. After that re-run, an external critique raised five points. edits.paragraph_text: The analysis is driven by scripts/run_all.sh. It comprises the nine numbered stages of the supplied pipeline, plus Stage 3a, written during this session to replace a failed VCF download, and Stage 3b, the supplied per-isolate quality-control script that run_all.sh labels as part of Stage 3 but that is given its own row in Table 3.1, and four stages added after review: Stage 10, a multiallelic-aware resistance marker panel; Stage 11, a diagnostic for the confounding of agro-ecological zone with sequencing study; Stage 12, which replaces Stage 10's marker panel entirely after an external critique showed that Stage 10's method of identifying markers — matching SnpEff protein-change strings against a hand-written list — could not see a resistance allele that is the reference residue and could not see a residue requiring two changes in one codon (both failures occurred); and Stage 13, which rebuilds the analysis matrix under six settings of the two thresholds that define the dataset and recomputes pairwise FST and the region-level Mantel test under each. Stage 13 is the stage whose result matters most, and it does not go the manuscript's way: it leaves near-panmixia stronger than before and it removes the support for isolation by distance, which is significant at the published thresholds and at almost none of the others. That is a loss of a result, not a refinement of one, and Section 3.14 states it as such. Stage 10 is retained in the repository and in Table 3.1 for the record, but no number in this manuscript now comes from it; Section 3.10 sets out the replacement method and Section 3.10.1 the reason it was needed. Stages run in order; each writes its outputs to disk so that a failure costs one stage rather than the whole run. That caching is stated here with its qualification rather than as a design virtue, because it was also the pipeline's most dangerous defect: the guards skipped a stage whenever its output file already existed, without checking whether the input had changed, so when the SNP panel moved from 3,359 to 3,916 SNPs, ADMIXTURE and TreeMix silently reported the previous day's results as "stage finished". Only Stage 8 carried an assertion that caught it. The guards now require the output to be newer than its input; Section 3.13 sets out what happened and what was changed. Stages 10 to 13 are read-only with respect to everything upstream: they create new output files and modify none, so no estimate in Sections 6.1 to 6.7 depends on them. Two further checks changed no stage's method but changed what the existing stages describe: Stage 3's three ordinations were re-run on the 1,900-isolate analysis set rather than the 4,905 pre-QC isolates (Section 3.4.1), and the 19 XtX outliers were audited against the Pf8 per-variant quality annotations (Section 3.11.1). This section describes each stage: what it does, why, what it assumes, and how it constrains what follows. Where a method changed in the corrected re-run, or in the rebuild that followed the external critique, or in these final checks, the change and its motivation are stated in place rather than relegated to a revision log.

edits.paragraph_text: [Observed] The cascade, defined once. Stage 10's panel held 44 canonical codon-allele records, covering 41 distinct protein changes, in eight of the nine panel genes (pfcoronin contributed none); 21 were polymorphic in these 1,900 isolates; 6 of the 21 survived the ingest mask — the in_genomewide_scan field, defined at step10_resistance_panel.py:349 as numalt == 1, i.e. "would have survived the ingest filter"; and 3 reached the MAF-filtered scan matrix: pfdhfr C59R, pfdhfr N51I and pfaat1 S258L. The other three that passed the mask — pfcrt I356T, pfmdr1 D1246Y and pfcrt N326S — were then cut by MAF ≥ 0.05 at frequencies of 0.016, 0.011 and 0.008. These four numbers (44, 21, 6, 3) carry exactly this meaning wherever they appear in this manuscript, and the Abstract, Table 1.1, Section 6.8.3, Table 6.8 and Section 10.1 use this wording. In particular, the genome-wide scan did test three of the 21 polymorphic canonical codons, and no pfcrt, pfmdr1, pfdhps or pfk13 codon reached the MAF-filtered scan matrix — pfdhps because nothing survived the ingest mask, the others because what survived was either too rare (pfcrt I356T, pfcrt N326S and pfmdr1 D1246Y all passed the mask, reached the genome-wide store and were then cut by MAF at 0.016, 0.011 and 0.008) or monomorphic here (six pfk13 codons — F446I, P441L, Y493H, P553L, R561H, A675V — passed the mask and were fetched and found invariant). "Could not test at all" would be true of the final MAF-filtered scan matrix but false of ascertainment, which is the distinction this paragraph exists to draw, so the stronger wording is not used.

edits.context_before: Isolation by distance is withdrawn as a supported result. Two checks now bear on this test, they vary different things, and they agree. The leave-one-region-out jackknife (Table 6.7) finds it significant in 4 of 7 replicates, with significance collapsing whenever the region defining either end of the distance range is dropped — Upper East at the long end, Greater Accra or Eastern at the short end. The threshold sensitivity (Table 6.7a) finds it significant in 2 of 6 scenarios, and the relaxation that most directly tests the filter doing the most work — removing the Fws cut, which more than doubles the isolate count to 4,403 — moves p from 0.0252 to 0.1792. The honest statement is that the isolation-by-distance result holds at the published thresholds and almost nowhere else. The original manuscript's "weak but detectable" distance effect, retained through every earlier revision of this section including the one that reported the jackknife improving from 2 of 7 to 4 of 7, cannot be retained now, and the grading of this result in Sections 1, 7 and 10 as supported or moderately supported must change with it. This is the only positive spatial finding in the analysis and it is the one that did not survive the two checks the audit identified as most needed. It is reported here in full rather than deleted — the point estimate at the published thresholds is unchanged and a reader is entitled to it — but it should not be cited as evidence of distance-limited gene flow in Ghana.
edits.context_after: [Interpreted] Three further qualifications apply to the Mantel tests themselves. First, the zone-level test has the larger correlation but the larger p-value, which is a power effect rather than a contradiction: with four populations only 4! = 24 distinct orderings exist, so the finest attainable p-value is 1/24 = 0.042 and significance requires essentially the single best permutation. The region-level test, with 5,040 orderings, is the better powered of the two and is the one reported above. Second, the zone-level p-value is reported as a Monte Carlo estimate from 9,999 permutations when the exact value is enumerable over all 24 orderings; this remains outstanding and the estimate should be replaced by the exact figure. Third, several of the 21 region pairs rest on small samples (Volta 21 isolates, Brong Ahafo 25, Eastern 34), and the scatter in Figure 6.4 is correspondingly wide.

This is the fourth consecutive round in which a correction contained its own defect. Each layer was checked for internal consistency against the project's own outputs, and that checking worked. edits.paragraph_text: [Interpreted] What it does not license, and what the previous draft got wrong. The previous draft went further and concluded that "sentinel surveillance at a small number of sites is an adequate design for detecting emergence — the samples do not need to be spatially comprehensive to be representative". That claim is withdrawn. It is unsupported by anything measured here, and it is contradicted by the mechanism this project's own literature review sets out: selection builds connectivity that neutral demography does not, so a selected haplotype can sweep across a region while the neutral background stays homogeneous — and, symmetrically, resistance-allele trajectories can remain site-specific even under neutral panmixia. Sentinel surveillance measures marker frequencies, not neutral structure. Low genome-wide neutral FST says nothing about whether marker frequencies at one site represent the country.
edits.context_before: [Interpreted] What the neutral result licenses. Neutral common-variant differentiation between zones is negligible — maximum pairwise FST 0.00232, with one of six confidence intervals spanning zero (Guinea savanna vs transitional zone, [−0.00083, 0.00178]), and the maximum staying within 0.00204–0.00255 across six threshold scenarios (Table 8.3) — so a spatially sparse design is adequate for characterising neutral structure. Marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and the rebuilt resistance panel shows significant between-zone variation at six of the nine panel genes, including pfdhfr, pfdhps and pfaat1 (the others being pfcrt, pfmdr1 and pfmdr2). If the question is whether a handful of sites will give a representative picture of the neutral genomic background, these data answer yes; if the question is whether those sites will give a representative picture of resistance-marker frequencies, these data answer no.
edits.context_after: [Observed] The resistance panel settles the question empirically, and the answer is no. Marker frequencies do differ by zone. pfaat1 S258L spans about 28 percentage points from coast to far north (0.824 to 0.544, χ² p = 1.89 × 10⁻¹⁸, n = 1,896 called). pfdhps G437 — the allele that was missing from the panel altogether in the previous draft — runs 0.964 in deciduous forest and 0.941 on the coast against 0.875 in Guinea savanna and 0.800 in the transitional zone (χ² p = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶, n = 1,892). The pfdhfr codons are heterogeneous across the four zones (S108N χ² p = 9.4 × 10⁻⁷; C59R 4.8 × 10⁻⁵; N51I 2.4 × 10⁻⁴) and the IRN triple-mutant haplotype itself runs 0.750 in Guinea savanna, 0.788 in deciduous forest, 0.867 on the coast and 0.880 in the transitional zone on 25 isolates. These are all four-zone heterogeneity tests; no directional south-versus-Guinea contrast was run, and the transitional zone's values rest on 25 isolates (§7.2). A sentinel site on the coast and a sentinel site in Upper East would report materially different resistance-marker profiles from the same panmictic parasite population. The operational implication is the reverse of the previous draft's: neutral structure can be characterised sparsely; marker frequencies cannot. A surveillance design intended to track resistance needs to span the gradient, and this analysis is evidence for rather than against that requirement.

edits.context_after: [Calculated] Robustness of the readings above to the corrected panel. The conclusions in this section were reached on a neutral panel that grew from 3,359 to 3,916 SNPs (+16.6 per cent) once the filter order was corrected, with stages 4 to 9 re-run on the larger matrix. The substantive readings held — near-panmixia, maximum pairwise FST of about 0.0023, and a near-flat cross-validation curve. One reading did not hold, though it failed a later check rather than this one: isolation by distance, described in earlier drafts as a weak, leverage-dependent but real distance effect, is significant in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and is now reported as not robust (§8, Table 8.3). Within the corrected run it had in fact improved — the Mantel result no longer depends on the undisclosed censoring, and significant jackknife replicates went 2 of 7 to 4 of 7 — which is a useful reminder that a result can be made more reproducible and still not be true. One result gained inferential support: TreeMix now reports m = 2 as a selected descriptive model on edge p-values instead of hedging, though the variance-explained criterion across the full sweep still prefers m = 3. The BayPass threshold, outlier count and gene list all moved (11.232 to 10.840; 15 to 19 outliers; 11 to 13 genes). The marker panel is a different matter: it was not re-run but rebuilt, by a new script that reconstructs codons rather than matching annotation strings, and several of its conclusions did change (§7.5, §8). This wording is used identically in §6 and in §8; details and the full comparison are in Table 8.1.

edits.paragraph_text: Whether the conclusions are stable under alternative Fws and MAF thresholds is no longer unresolved. It was tested on 10 October 2026 (scripts/step13_sensitivity.py, Table 10.1) and answered in both directions: near-panmixia is stable, with max FST ranging only 0.00204–0.00255 over six scenarios, and isolation by distance is not, being significant in two of the six. edits.context_before: Whether any apparent zone effect survives control for administrative region, collection year and sequencing study. Not resolvable with these data (Section 9.2). Study is a fourth confounder added since the original draft: four of the six zone pairs share no sequencing study at all, including coastal savanna against Guinea savanna, the pair behind every headline number. That overlap is computed on the 4,905 QC-passing isolates and was not recomputed on the 1,900-isolate analysis set (see the denominator note in Section 10.1).
edits.context_after: Whether Ghanaian Plasmodium falciparum shows isolation by distance at all. This has moved out of the answered column and into this one. A Mantel correlation that appears at one setting of the two thresholds and vanishes at four others is not evidence either way, and 21 pairs from seven administrative regions is a thin test on which to rest a spatial claim. edits.paragraph_text: Test isolation by distance properly, or stop reporting it as a finding. The region-level Mantel test on 21 pairs is at the limit of what Pf8's Ghanaian metadata supports, and it fails at four of the six threshold settings tried. Re-running it will not help. Two routes would: district- or site-level coordinates wherever the metadata carries them, which raises both the number of populations and the number of pairs; and a continuous-space method that does not require populations to be defined at all. Either is a new analysis rather than a robustness check, and neither is cheap. Until one is done the manuscript should carry near-panmixia as its spatial result and isolation by distance only as a non-robust observation, which is how Section 10.1 and Table 10.2 now report it.

edits.context_after: Reframe the thesis objectives in light of the collinearity, and in light of Objective 3 now being answered. The question "do ecological zones structure the parasite population?" cannot be answered with Pf8 metadata alone. Two questions that can be, and have been, are "is Ghanaian P. falciparum spatially structured at all, and what does that imply for surveillance design?" and "do resistance-marker frequencies vary across the country?" edits.quote: [Interpreted] A closing assessment. The analysis has done what a baseline characterisation should do: established the scale of structure, found it to be small, identified precisely which design features limit what can be inferred, and produced a short candidate list for follow-up. What has changed across the three rounds is the standing of the negative results, the standing of our own corrections, and now the standing of a positive result. The absence of resistance loci from the outlier scan was not a result at all but a filter artefact, and correcting it converted the thesis's third objective from a null finding into its best-supported positive one — pfdhps G437 at 0.897 and zone-structured, the pfdhfr triple mutant measured as a haplotype at 0.771, and pfaat1 S258L as a strong candidate whose demonstrated functional effect is modest and background-dependent. The absence of artemisinin resistance is now genuinely tested, across the complete WHO-validated and candidate sets, on 1,845 to 1,876 called isolates per codon over 2009–2021, and genuinely negative. But the first correction of the panel was itself wrong in four ways, and only an external reader caught it. The honest conclusion is therefore two claims rather than one. A negative result is worth nothing until the thing it denies has been shown to be measurable. And internal consistency is not correctness: every defect in the first corrected panel came from a list, a direction or a label taken on trust, and the verification architecture built to catch stale numbers was never built to ask whether the inputs were the right ones. The third round adds a third claim, and it is the least comfortable of the three. Four checks this list carried as outstanding were run, and the one previously described here as addressing "the two most likely reviewer objections" removed a finding instead of answering them: isolation by distance survives neither a relaxation of the monoclonality cut nor a lower MAF floor, and is significant at two of six threshold settings. The gain and the loss come from the same six runs. The check that destroyed the spatial finding is the check that made near-panmixia the best-evidenced conclusion in the manuscript, because FST moved by less than 0.0005 while the Mantel p-value crossed 0.05 four times. A result that holds only at the thresholds that produced it was never a result; it was a setting. The manuscript is shorter by one finding and better by one method, and the third claim is simply that: a threshold is a hypothesis, and until it has been varied, every conclusion downstream of it is conditional on a number nobody tested.

edits.paragraph_text: [Observed] Session decisions versus inherited defaults. Of the 28 rows above, 27 are values in force and the twenty-eighth records the sensitivity grid rather than a setting. Of the 27, five are session decisions taken during this analysis and carry no external justification — CLONAL_THRESHOLD, MIN_GENOTYPE_GQ, TREEMIX_BLOCK_SIZE, BayPass NVAL and the codon panel's mixed-call policy — and two more, TSNE_PERPLEXITY and PCOA_N_AXES, are additions rather than judgements. Three are corrections forced by the internal audit (TreeMix SE, BayPass NTHREADS, the XtX q-value thresholds) and three by the external critique (the GENES list, the HAPLOTYPES definitions and the codon-panel ALT restriction), and all six are marked as such — six in total, not the seven stated in the previous version, whose count did not match the marks actually carried in the table; MAX_MISSING is unchanged in value but changed position in the filtering cascade, which is why the SNP count moved. The remainder are pipeline defaults or thesis-workflow specifications. The rows that most affect reported numbers are MIN_GENOTYPE_GQ, which governs the size of the SNP panel; BayPass NTHREADS, which governs whether the outlier scan is reproducible at all; and the codon panel's GENES list, which governs whether a marker exists in the manuscript or not — a point made the hard way, since pfdhps 437 was missing from the previous version because of how markers were identified rather than because of any threshold. Two of those rows have since been varied rather than merely justified: MIN_FWS and MIN_MAF were both relaxed in the sensitivity round, and the outcome is in Table 10.1 — near-panmixia unaffected, isolation by distance not surviving. MIN_GENOTYPE_GQ, which the paragraph above names as the largest discretionary choice in the pipeline, has still not been varied, and it governs the size of the SNP panel that every one of those six scenarios was drawn from.
edits.context_before: PI_MAF is not a MAF filter. The original text described the POD as "100,000 MAF-matched simulated SNPs". That is not what pi.maf does. In baypass_utils.R it truncates the simulated ancestral frequency to [0.05, 0.95] and binomial sampling then freely produces observed minor-allele frequencies below 0.05, so the POD is not matched to the observed MAF >= 0.05 spectrum. 0.05 is also simulate.baypass's own default, so setting it changed nothing. The "MAF-matched" wording has been removed from Sections 5.6, 6.8 and 8.1 as well as from this table. Section 6.8 had carried it in different words — "with the same MAF filter as the observed data" — which survived two earlier correction rounds precisely because those rounds searched for the phrase rather than for the claim; it has now been removed as well. The pseudo-observed set is not MAF-matched.

edits.quote: [Observed] This appendix exists for traceability, and it now records three rounds. Round one, 9–10 October 2026: an adversarial multi-agent audit. Eight reviewers working across separate dimensions raised 110 findings, each of which was then put to three independent verifiers prompted to refute it and defaulting to refuted where they could not substantiate the claim. A finding counts as confirmed only where at least two of three verifiers failed to refute it after checking the code, data or outputs themselves. Sixty-one findings were confirmed — 14 high severity, 31 medium, 16 low — with 19 disputed and 21 refuted. Thirty verifications in the reproducibility dimension were lost to a rate limit and are recorded as unverified rather than confirmed. Seven confirmed defects required code changes; stages 4 to 9 were re-run on 10 October 2026 with all seven in place. Round two, 10 October 2026: an external critique of the corrected manuscript. It raised five points. All five were upheld and four were defects in the analysis code, not in the prose — in the resistance panel that round one had introduced to fix its own largest finding. The panel was rebuilt as scripts/step12_codon_panel.py and every resistance number in this revision was read from that script's outputs. This is the fourth consecutive round in which a correction contained its own defect, and the pattern is consistent: each layer was checked for internal consistency against our own outputs, and what escaped was external correctness — whether the marker list matched an authoritative source, whether the annotation direction matched the reference genome, whether a co-occurrence claim had co-occurrence data behind it. The verification architecture was built to catch stale numbers, and it did. It was not built to ask whether the inputs were the right ones. Round three, 10 October 2026: the four outstanding robustness checks. This round was not an audit of the manuscript but the execution of four items that Section 10.4 carried as outstanding, and it is recorded here because one of them overturned a conclusion instead of confirming it. The Fws and MAF sensitivity analysis (scripts/step13_sensitivity.py) withdrew isolation by distance as a supported result — significant in two of six threshold scenarios — and, from the same six runs, made near-panmixia the best-evidenced conclusion in the manuscript. The outlier quality check cleared the exported-protein artefact concern and downgraded two chromosome-11 SNPs on an ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff signal. Stage 3 was re-run on the analysis set. The GeoJSON provenance cannot be closed analytically and remains open. Round three found no defect in the prose and none in the analysis code; what it found was that a published result depended on the thresholds that produced it. Two integrity incidents occurred during the round and are registered as rows 13 and 14 of Table F.1 rather than left in the logs.

remaining_keyword_occurrences_after_prop.text: [Interpreted] Conclusion. At the resolution these data permit, Ghanaian P. falciparum shows very low but statistically detectable differentiation at the retained common variants. Five of the six pairwise estimates have 95% confidence intervals excluding zero; only Guinea savanna against the transitional zone, where n = 25, spans it. Very low is not the same as undetectable, and neither is a demonstration of random mating, for which these data contain no direct evidence. What the sensitivity analysis adds is stability of the magnitude rather than absence of the effect: the maximum pairwise FST stays within 0.00204-0.00255 across all six threshold scenarios, over 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs, so the headline result is insensitive to both of the cuts that define the dataset. The companion claim does not survive the same treatment. The region-level isolation-by-distance result is significant at the published thresholds and at MAF >= 0.02, but in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, and this report therefore no longer asserts a distance effect, weak or otherwise. What remains of the spatial signal is a single south-to-north contrast, visible in the FST ranking and in the K = 2 minor component, with no robust evidence that genetic distance scales with geographic distance. That very low differentiation is a statement about neutral common-variant structure only: neutral common-variant differentiation between zones is negligible, so a spatially sparse design is adequate for characterising neutral structure, but marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and the resistance panel in this analysis shows significant between-zone variation at p < 0.001 at pfdhfr, pfdhps and pfaat1. That threshold is stated because it is a selection: on the four-zone chi-square as reported, several further loci are nominally significant at p < 0.05, among them pfcrt I356T (p = 1.6 x 10 to the -3), pfmdr2 I492V (p = 0.020) and pfmdr1 N86Y (p = 0.029). Low neutral FST therefore does not license an assumption that marker frequencies are spatially representative. The pfk13 result is a genuine tested negative - no screened resistance allele occurs at any of the 23 codons, which cover the complete WHO-validated set of 14 and all 6 candidates: twenty-two are fixed at the reference residue and codon 458 is at 0.9995 on a single Asn458Asp call, which is not the validated N458Y, on 1,845 to 1,876 isolates called per codon - rather than an untested absence; it is also a statement about 2009-2021 and not about current parasite populations. The XtX set remains a ranked candidate list, of which 13 SNPs survive FDR 10% and two adjacent chromosome-11 sites - one of them the fifth-ranked SNP overall - are flagged lower confidence on ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff grounds. All zone-level results describe a compound variable in which ecology, administrative region, collection period and sequencing study cannot be separated; that is a property of the Pf8 metadata, not of the analysis.

remaining_keyword_occurrences_after_prop.text: [Interpreted] Robustness of these conclusions to the corrected re-runs and the final checks. The population-structure readings held on a 16.6% larger SNP panel (3,359 to 3,916 SNPs) with corrected filter ordering, a bitwise-reproducible single-threaded BayPass, seeded permutation tests and full false-discovery accounting: very low differentiation at retained common variants, maximum FST of approximately 0.0023, and a near-flat ADMIXTURE cross-validation curve. First, the fitted quantity is six off-diagonal between-population covariances, and an unrooted four-taxon tree already uses five branch-length parameters, so m = 0 has one residual degree of freedom and m = 1 has none or fewer. A rise in variance explained from 0.897 to 0.941 between those two models is not by itself evidence of gene flow, and the original manuscript's treatment of the m = 0 to m = 1 improvement as "the one substantive result" applied a degrees-of-freedom argument against m = 3 while exempting m = 1 from it. The edge p-values are the stronger evidence precisely because they do not depend on the variance-explained curve. Second, with four populations, three of which are a single administrative region each, these edges cannot be read as specific geographic gene-flow corridors. What the graph establishes is narrower than it looks: within this fitted covariance model, a strictly bifurcating topology leaves residual covariance that two admixture edges absorb, and those two edges carry weights distinguishable from zero conditional on that graph. Edge significance is conditional on a fixed topology and root and does not propagate error in the graph structure itself (Pickrell and Pritchard 2012), so this is a statement about model fit rather than a demonstration of ongoing exchange. Those are conditional edge statistics, not identified directions of historical exchange.
